## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Real quarterly indexes to Parquet, locally
      Objective: Download a small real range of archived quarterly master indexes and turn it into canonical Parquet rows.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: an SEC identity (organization and contact email) from your partner (§7 step 1)
      Produces: a local downloader and parser emitting the sec-index-v1 row contract; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — raw bytes for each quarter in the chosen small range are kept with their SHA-256 values. O3 — those quarters yield Parquet rows that meet §4.5's row contract. The findings file records the measured cost of the real run: bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, request count and observed request rate.
      Leaves out: source manifest and checkpoints → Stage 3; replay → Stage 3; shared request lease → Stage 4; configuration validation → Stage 4; versioned publication → Stage 5; reconciliation → Stage 6; Azure deployment → Stage 7; scheduling and alerts → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily discovery and catch-up
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily indexes from a handoff date through the same downloader and parser.
      Outcomes: O2, O5
      Consumes: Stage 1 downloader and parser
      Produces: listing-based discovery for quarterly and daily sources; one shared code path
      Exit: O2 — real daily indexes from a handoff date join the catalog, and baseline overlap is deduplicated. O2 — fixtures pass §6 Discovery and coverage. O5 — backfill and daily runs call the same downloader and parser.
      Leaves out: source manifest and checkpoints → Stage 3; shared request lease → Stage 4; scheduling and alerts → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Source manifest, checkpoints and replay
      Objective: Make every source file a durable checkpoint unit and let parser changes replay from stored bytes.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stages 1–2
      Produces: source manifest and checkpoints (§4.5 records); content-addressed raw and observation paths; run reports (§4.7)
      Exit: O6 — §6 Replay passes: replay with SEC access disabled yields the same logical catalog, and a partial run resumes without losing completed units.
      Leaves out: shared request lease → Stage 4; versioned publication → Stage 5
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Shared request lease and configuration validation
      Objective: Put all SEC access under one lease and budget, and validate configuration before any I/O.
      Outcomes: O8, O11
      Consumes: Stage 3 source manifest and checkpoints
      Produces: shared request lease; configuration validation per §4.8 and §5
      Exit: O8 — §6 Access passes. O11 — every §5 Configuration error is refused before external I/O.
      Leaves out: Azure deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Versioned publication
      Objective: Publish complete quarter generations through a conditional active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 3 source manifest and checkpoints
      Produces: versioned publication: generations, manifests, change reports, active pointer
      Exit: O9 — §6 Publication passes, including the crash-injection and competing-publisher cases.
      Leaves out: reconciliation → Stage 6
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and gated withdrawals
      Objective: Re-read quarterly sources, apply safe changes, and gate withdrawals behind approval bound to the source hash.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stages 4–5
      Produces: reconciliation; withdrawal approval records
      Exit: O7 — §6 Reconciliation passes for additions, updates and open-quarter absence. O10 — a closed-quarter removal stays `awaiting_approval` until approval names its hash.
      Leaves out: scheduling and alerts → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure deployment
      Objective: Deploy the shared worker and pipelines to an isolated Azure environment, with triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 1–6; ADR and spec accepted (§7 step 1)
      Produces: Azure deployment (§4.9 infra, identities, ADF pipelines, jobs); integration tests on isolated Azure (§6); smoke-test record
      Exit: O4 — §7 steps 3–5 are done, and the smoke test records bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, image digest, request rate and Azure cost.
      Leaves out: scheduling and alerts → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Baseline and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the full backfill and daily catch-up, then enable schedules, alerts and runbooks.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7 (production run)
      Consumes: Stage 7 Azure deployment
      Produces: scheduling and alerts; runbooks (§8); release record
      Exit: §7 steps 6–9 are done, and every §7 Exit bullet is observed, including scheduled executions.

      ROUTING: writing-plans
